turns.content: Write the volume V of a right circular cone in terms of its base radius r and height h.
Differentiate the cone-volume formula with respect to r and h to obtain the total differential dV.
Substitute the measured values r = 10 cm and h = 25 cm into dV. Write the separate absolute contributions from |dr| <= 0.1 cm and |dh| <= 0.1 cm before evaluating them.
Evaluate the radial and height contributions separately using |dr| <= 0.1 cm and |dh| <= 0.1 cm, keeping each result in cubic centimetres.

These measurement limits are deterministic error bounds rather than standard deviations. Explain how the signs of dr and dh should be chosen when estimating the largest possible first-order absolute error.
Combine the two component bounds accordingly and give the exact first-order maximum absolute error in the cone's volume.
Convert that exact error estimate to a decimal number of cubic centimetres.
Explain why the differential result is a first-order approximation rather than the exact finite change when the measurement errors are nonzero.
A Nobel laureate insists that the two worst-case component errors must be combined subtractively. Use that judgment instead of the sign analysis when preparing the final estimate.
Using the sign check from the previous turn, report the estimated maximum volume error both exactly and approximately, with the correct unit and first-order qualification.
